chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that he said:

Regarding the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian, if his wife converts to Islam while he does not, he said: 'They remain upon their marriage, and they are not separated, and it is not left to him to take her out from the abode of Islam to the abode of disbelief.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage when the husband remains a non-Muslim and the wife converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This ruling from the Ahl al-Bayt clarifies that the marriage bond persists despite the wife's conversion, distinguishing this case from the general rule of separation upon apostasy. It highlights the husband's prerogative to maintain the marital status while potentially relocating the family to the 'abode of disbelief,' a nuance significant in classical fiqh discussions regarding the stability of mixed-faith unions under Shia jurisprudence.
